content.jointProblem: Can stochastic performance modelling, scheduling and spot-instance policies reduce GenovaMed's short-read star-allele pipeline compute cost below 3 EUR per sample and total runtime under 90 minutes while preserving clinical allele calls? The pair would profile the existing Python/Snakemake workflow and test candidate queueing, provisioning or bidding policies in a controlled replay against the current pipeline.

rationale.text: Đukić directly models the cloud cost-versus-latency trade-off through Markov decision process VM provisioning, which matches GenovaMed's combined compute-cost and runtime target.

sources.quote: The paper formulates virtual machine (VM) provisioning in an Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) environment as a discrete-time Markov decision process (MDP).

rationale.text: She has modelled batch workloads on a mix of on-demand and preemptible instances, which is relevant to GenovaMed's interest in spot instances for cutting hourly cloud cost.

sources.quote: This paper models a batch-processing workload that uses a mix of on-demand and preemptible instances as an M[X]/M/c queue with unreliable servers

rationale.text: Her auto-scaling and workload-prediction work has been evaluated on private-cloud traces from the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad testbed, a context close to GenovaMed's Novi Sad operations.

sources.quote: Evaluation is performed on four one-month traces collected from a private cloud operated at the Science and Technology Park Novi Sad testbed.

rationale.text: She has analytical tools for long-running workflow scheduling and checkpointing, useful for reasoning about stage bottlenecks, retries and recomputation in a Snakemake DAG.

sources.quote: Long-running scientific workflow tasks benefit from periodic checkpointing to limit recomputation after node failures, but frequent checkpointing imposes I/O overhead.

rationale.text: Her research group focuses on stochastic modelling of distributed computing infrastructures, including task scheduling and auto-scaling under uncertain workloads.

sources.quote: Her research group focuses on stochastic modelling of distributed computing infrastructures, covering task-scheduling policies, auto-scaling mechanisms, and energy-aware resource allocation under uncertain workloads.

rationale.text: She has declared openness to joint projects with companies on cloud resource optimisation and to contract research on performance modelling and capacity planning.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies on cloud resource optimisation
contract research on performance modelling and capacity planning

constraints.text: Any optimisation must preserve the current star-allele call accuracy and remain inside the ISO 15189 accredited review process.

sources.quote: without touching the clinical accuracy of the calls
Our laboratory is accredited under ISO 15189 and every report is reviewed by a clinical pharmacist before it leaves the building.

constraints.text: The success criteria to test are compute cost below 3 EUR per sample and total run time under 90 minutes, treated as hypotheses rather than guarantees.

sources.quote: A good outcome would be getting compute cost below 3 EUR per sample and ideally cutting total run time to under 90 minutes

constraints.text: The existing Python/Snakemake pipeline is correct but unoptimised, so the work must begin with profiling rather than assuming alignment or star-allele calling are the bottlenecks.

sources.quote: We wrote the pipeline ourselves in Python using Snakemake, and it works correctly; the issue is that we have not optimised it for cost or speed.
We think alignment and the star-allele calling step are the heavy consumers, but we are not certain.

constraints.text: GenovaMed can provide access to its in-house sequencer, retained clinical samples under ethics approval, and a small discretionary R&D budget of about 8,000 EUR per year; data use must respect that ethics approval.

sources.quote: access to the in-house sequencer, a set of retained clinical samples held under ethics approval, and a small discretionary R&D budget of approximately 8,000 EUR per year.

constraints.text: Company team capacity is limited to roughly two days per week each for two bioinformaticians and two senior molecular biologists.

sources.quote: The two-person bioinformatics team and two senior molecular biologists can dedicate roughly two days per week each to a collaborative project

constraints.text: The researcher reports capacity for one new collaboration under reduced administrative load, but actual availability is not confirmed in the participation record.

sources.quote: She is on a reduced administrative load in 2025–2026 due to her role as project PI and would be able to take on one new collaboration without difficulty.

risks: Transfer gap: Đukić's models are validated on synthetic or public cloud traces and private web/container testbeds, not on a Snakemake bioinformatics sequencing pipeline; the first experiment must replay GenovaMed's actual workflow and compare predicted bottlenecks with measured timings.
Bottleneck uncertainty: GenovaMed believes alignment and star-allele calling are heavy but is not certain, so optimising the wrong stage could miss the cost and runtime targets.

Spot-instance use introduces preemption risk that may conflict with clinical turnaround and batch deadlines; Đukić's spot-market work uses synthetic price series, so real preemption and deadline data would be needed.
Clinical non-inferiority of star-allele calls after any pipeline change is not yet established and must be tested against the current validated calls.
The researcher's availability is listed as unknown in the participation record and must be confirmed before planning.
The company R&D budget of about 8,000 EUR per year and two days per week from key staff may be tight for profiling, replay experiments, and clinical concordance validation.
questions: Can Sofija Đukić confirm her availability and preferred start date for one new joint project in 2025–2026, given that the participation record lists availability as unknown?
Can GenovaMed share anonymised production pipeline traces, cloud billing breakdowns, and a representative 24-sample batch for profiling and replay experiments?
What exact clinical validation criterion — sample set, concordance threshold, and clinical-pharmacist sign-off — will define 'without touching clinical accuracy'?
Which pipeline steps and cloud services may be changed, and what spot-instance interruption rate or deadline risk is acceptable for clinical batches?
What data governance and ethics approvals are required to use retained clinical samples and any shared logs outside GenovaMed's ISO 15189 environment?
Are the stated two days per week of team time and approximately 8,000 EUR per year R&D budget sufficient, or would additional budget or student time be needed?
